newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones reports drop in profits.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones reports drop in profits.

text.p: Dow Jones & Co. reported a 32.5 percent drop in first-quarter profits Wednesday, citing a plunge in operating income at its financial information unit and predicting lower earnings for the year.
Dow Jones, which publishes The Wall Street Journal, said earnings fell to $25.3 million, or 27 cents a share, from $37.6 million, or 39 cents a share, in the year-ago quarter.

"Earnings for the first quarter were in line with the company's expectations," company Chairman Peter Kann said in a statement, warning that profits for the year would fall to $1.20 to $1.40 a share. Dow Jones earned $190 million, or $1.96 a share, in 1996.
The company's first-quarter earnings exceeded the consensus Wall Street analysts' prediction of 24 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks analyst forecasts.
The financial information and news company's also announced it was reducing the bonuses paid to top managers for 1996.
Revenues grew 3.6 percent to $606 million from $585 million a year ago, the company said.
The earnings report came a day after the company announced an alliance with software giant Microsoft Corp. to develop information and transaction systems for financial institutions.

Dow Jones said the initiative was part of its already announced plan to spend $650 million over four years revamping its struggling Dow Jones Markets financial information service, formerly known as Telerate. Dow Jones Markets' main competitors are Reuters Holdings Plc and Bloomberg LP.
Kahn said the $650 million programme and the near-term outlook for Dow Jones Markets would lower earnings for the year.
First-quarter revenues included a 4.4 percent drop in revenues from financial information services -- including Dow Jones Markets and Dow Jones Newswires -- to $266 million from $278 million.
But financial information services' operating income took an even bigger hit, falling 83.8 percent to $7.47 million from $46.1 million, Dow Jones said.

However, the company reported an 11 percent increase in revenues to $309.3 million from $278.5 million from its business publishing segment, including the Journal, Barron's weekly and other publications, television and online operations. Operating income nearly doubled to $50.4 million.
Its Ottaway Newspapers community newspaper unit's revenue grew 5.4 percent to $68 million from $64.5 million.
Dow Jones stock dropped 75 cents to $40 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
